chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who fights to protect his wealth, so he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'Whoever is killed defending his wealth is in the rank of the martyr.'
We asked him, 'Is it better to fight?' He said, 'If he does not fight, there is no harm. As for me, if I had not fought and they had left me (with my wealth), [I would have been blameworthy].'

key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةِ الشَّهِيدِ: in the rank/status of the martyr
key_terms.فَلاَ بَأْسَ: there is no harm (it is permissible)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling for someone killed while defending their property?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that defending one's property against aggression grants the status of martyrdom, a ruling derived from the Prophet’s statement. The dialogue further explores the virtue of active defense, where the Imam affirms that while abstaining is permissible, he personally preferred to fight to preserve his wealth, highlighting the Shia emphasis on the dignity of material rights alongside spiritual merit.
